## 9e7fcd5605d8

**Concrete semantic counterexample:** the generator equates “component does not fill its bounding box” with “component has an enclosed hole.” The canonical rule instead flood-fills background regions inside the component bounding box and treats only regions not connected to the bounding-box boundary as holes.

A 3×3 open U-shaped component is enough to separate them (shown inside a 5×5 background):

```text
00000
02020
02020
02220
00000
```

The center background is connected to the exterior through the top opening, so the canonical rule has **no enclosed hole** and should recolor the component to 4:

```text
00000
04040
04040
04440
00000
```

The generator's `_solid_hollow_counts` sees bounding-box area 9 versus 7 component cells and classifies it as hollow, implying color 8. The ordinary distribution never exposes this disagreement because it emits only filled rectangles and closed rectangle outlines. Thus a shortcut “non-rectangle → 8; filled rectangle → 4” can fit all generated lessons while failing the canonical topology rule. The same generator also declares `n_distinct_colors` and `palette_size` up to 3 but always emits one shared input color; for seeds 0–4 with `n_distinct_colors=3, palette_size=3`, every generated grid still had exactly one nonzero color.
